evals.prompt: Review PR 2075 for the extension listing
evals.expected_output: Structured review of gbt9704 extension with APPROVE verdict. Should check duplicate, repo, README, license, category, quality, and security. Repo is public, MIT licensed, has README, correct category (custom-formats.yml).

assertions.description: Output contains APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, or INVESTIGATE verdict
Output mentions duplicate check
Output mentions license check
Output mentions README check
Output mentions security scan
Verdict is APPROVE (repo is clean, MIT, has README, correct category)
Output names the repository

evals.prompt: Review PR 2074 for the extension listing
evals.expected_output: Structured review of shortiquiz and stepbystep extensions. Two entries from same author. Should check both, run security scan on each, return per-entry verdicts. PR verdict is the worst across both entries.

assertions.description: Output mentions both shortiquiz and stepbystep
Output contains a verdict
Security check appears for both entries
License checked for at least one entry
Duplicate check ran

evals.prompt: Review PR 2162 for the extension listing
evals.expected_output: Review of the index extension (jmgirard/quarto-index). All mechanical checks pass, it uses the MIT license, and the category is correct. The review must explain that Quarto's native indexing is PDF-only through raw LaTeX and makeidx, so the extension fills a gap rather than duplicating a built-in feature. Quarto CLI discussion 3849 is the canonical open feature request. The verdict is APPROVE, with the repository's recent creation reported as context rather than a finding.

assertions.description: Verdict is APPROVE
Says what problem the extension solves, not just that it is valid
Identifies that native Quarto indexing is PDF-only
Names the native mechanism rather than asserting a gap vaguely
Finds the canonical upstream discussion
Reports repo age or lack of users as context, not as a blocking finding
Uses textual verdict words the template requires

evals.prompt: Review a listing PR adding an extension whose repository has no LICENSE file, no license detected by GitHub, and no license section in its README.
evals.expected_output: The listing requirements demand an open-source license, so this cannot be APPROVE. Expected REQUEST_CHANGES naming the missing license, and a contributor comment draft asking for one. Must not silently downgrade to a warning and approve.

assertions.description: Verdict is not a bare APPROVE
Asks for changes or investigation
License is named as the reason
Produces a contributor comment draft

evals.prompt: Review a listing PR where the GitHub API returns a rate-limit error partway through the checks.
evals.expected_output: Failed lookups must be reported as UNVERIFIED and the remaining checks completed. A rate-limited call must not be reported as a missing README, a missing license or a deleted repository, and the PR must not be approved on the strength of checks that never ran.

assertions.description: Does not approve on the strength of checks that never ran
Uses an unverified state rather than inferring absence
Does not claim the README or repo is missing
Other checks still reported
Recommends investigation or changes rather than approval

notes: scripts/self-test.sh covers deterministic behavior: regex metacharacters in names, repository path prefixes, extension discovery when directory and repository names differ, vendored documentation copies, ordering, and cross-file consistency. These evals cover judgments that require a model.
